content: The guideline development process involved external experts and WHO staff, with contributions from members of the Evidence and Recommendation Review Groups (ERRGs). These groups were divided into three domains: Clinical Services, Service Delivery, and Law and Policy. Each domain had its own panel of experts, whose names, affiliations, areas of expertise, and declarations of interest were documented. Clinical Services Domain 1. Laura Castleman: Affiliated with Planned Parenthood Michigan and the University of Michigan, based in Ann Arbor, MI, USA (Americas region). Expertise in obstetrics and gynecology. No conflicts of interest declared. 2. Suchitra Dalvie: Consultant for sexual and reproductive health programs, based in Mumbai, India (South-East Asia region). Expertise in abortion and advocacy. No conflicts of interest declared. 3. Michalina Drejza: Member of the International Youth Alliance for Family Planning (IYAFP), based in Poznań, Poland (Europe region). Expertise in obstetrics, gynecology, and youth health. No conflicts of interest declared. 4. Kristina Gemzell Danielsson: Head of the Department of Women’s and Children’s Health at Karolinska Institutet, Stockholm, Sweden (Europe region). Expertise in obstetrics, gynecology, and abortion research. No conflicts of interest declared. 5. Laura Gil: Clinician at Fundación Educación Para la Salud Reproductiva (ESAR), Bogotá, Colombia (Americas region). Expertise in abortion and contraception. No conflicts of interest declared. 6. Selma Hajri: Founder and President of the TAWHIDA Group for Research and Action on Women’s Health, based in Tunis, Tunisia (Eastern Mediterranean region). Expertise in abortion, contraception, and research. No conflicts of interest declared. 7. Guyo Jaldesa: Associate Professor of Obstetrics and Gynecology at the University of Nairobi, Kenya (Africa region). Expertise in obstetrics and gynecology. No conflicts of interest declared. 8. Dhammika Perera: Affiliated with Marie Stopes International, based in London, UK (Europe region). Expertise in abortion and contraception. No conflicts of interest declared. 9. Alongkone Phengsavanh: Vice Dean at the University of Health Sciences, Vientiane, Lao People’s Democratic Republic (Western Pacific region). Expertise in obstetrics, gynecology, and abortion care. No conflicts of interest declared. 10. Judiac Ranapea: Department of Health, Cape Town, South Africa (Africa region). Expertise in nursing, nurse training, and abortion care. No conflicts of interest declared. 11. Kitihoun Serge: Reproductive Health Unit, Alfred Comlan Quenum Regional Institute of Public Health, Ouidah, Benin (Africa region). Expertise in abortion and contraception. No conflicts of interest declared. 12. Christina Zampas: Center for Reproductive Rights, Geneva, Switzerland (Europe region). Expertise in law, human rights, sex work, and forced sterilization. No conflicts of interest declared. Additional contributors to the scoping meetings for this domain included experts such as Abigail Aiken (University of Texas, USA), Rodica Comendant (Reproductive Health Training Center, Moldova), Debora Diniz (Instituto de Bioética, Brazil), Angel Foster (University of Ottawa, Canada), Daniel Grossman (University of California, San Francisco, USA), and others. Service Delivery Domain 1. Fauzia Akhter Huda: Project Coordinator at the Maternal and Child Health Division, International Centre for Diarrhoeal Disease Research, Dhaka, Bangladesh (South-East Asia region). Expertise in public health, health systems, and abortion. No conflicts of interest declared. 2. Nana Yaa Appiah: Women’s Voices Foundation, Accra, Ghana (Africa region). Expertise in pharmacy, social marketing, and professional development. No conflicts of interest declared. 3. Karla Berdichevsky: Director of Gender Equity and Reproductive Health, Mexico Federal Ministry of Health, Mexico City, Mexico (Americas region). Expertise in sexual and reproductive health programming, policy, and research. No conflicts of interest declared. 4. Jemima Araba Dennis-Antwi: Ghana College of Nurses and Midwives, Accra, Ghana (Africa region). Expertise in health systems strengthening, maternal health, midwifery, and nursing training. No conflicts of interest declared. 5. Surendra Dhital: Independent pharmacist, Kathmandu, Nepal (South-East Asia region). Expertise in pharmacy, counseling, and safe abortion. No conflicts of interest declared. 6. Caitlin Gerdts: Vice President for Research at Ibis Reproductive Health, Oakland, CA, USA (Americas region). Expertise in qualitative research, technology use, and access to abortion. No conflicts of interest declared. 7. Daniel Maciera: Economics Department, University of Buenos Aires, Argentina (Americas region). Expertise in health systems research, health programming, and policy development. No conflicts of interest declared. 8. Vinoj Manning: CEO of Ipas Development Foundation, New Delhi, India (South-East Asia region). Expertise in health systems and abortion care. No conflicts of interest declared. 9. Sybil Nkeiru: Generation Initiative for Women and Youth Network (GIWYN), Lagos, Nigeria (Africa region). Expertise in human rights activism. No conflicts of interest declared. 10. Hiromi Obara: Deputy Director, Division of Global Health Policy and Research, National Center for Global Health and Medicine, Tokyo, Japan (Western Pacific region). Expertise in health planning, management, maternal health, and abortion policy. No conflicts of interest declared. 11. Karan Parikh: International Youth Alliance for Family Planning (IYAFP), Mumbai, India (South-East Asia region). Expertise as a clinician and youth health advocate. No conflicts of interest declared. 12. Michelle Remme: Research Lead at the United Nations University’s International Institute for Global Health (UNU-IIGH), Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia (Western Pacific region). Expertise in research, gender, and health system financing. No conflicts of interest declared. Additional contributors to the scoping meetings for this domain included Patrick Aboagye (Ghana Health Services, Ghana), Laura Castleman (Ipas, Planned Parenthood, and University of Michigan, USA), Amanda Cleeve (Karolinska Institutet, Sweden), and others. Law and Policy Domain 1. Marge Berer: Coordinator of the International Campaign for Women’s Right to Safe Abortion, London, UK (Europe region). Expertise in social science and abortion policy. No conflicts of interest declared. 2. Joanna Erdman: Associate Professor at the Schulich School of Law, Dalhousie University, Halifax, Canada (Americas region). Expertise in human rights, health law, and policy. No conflicts of interest declared. 3. Godfrey Kangaude: Postdoctoral Researcher at the University of Pretoria and Fellow in Reproductive and Sexual Health Law at the University of Toronto, Malawi (Africa region). Expertise in sexual and reproductive health and rights law. No conflicts of interest declared. 4. Akila Radhakrishnan: President of the Global Justice Center, New York, USA (Americas region). Expertise in law and policy. No conflicts of interest declared. 5. Ruben Avila Reyna: Member of the International Youth Alliance for Family Planning (IYAFP), Nuevo León, Mexico (Americas region). Expertise in human rights, advocacy, and youth health. No conflicts of interest declared. 6. Chi-Chi Undie: Senior Associate at the Population Council, Nairobi, Kenya (Africa region). Expertise in abortion, contraception, and policy. No conflicts of interest declared. 7. Abhijit Das: Center for Health and Social Justice, New Delhi, India (South-East Asia region). Expertise in human rights. No conflicts of interest declared. 8. Sara Hossain: Supreme Court of Bangladesh, Dhaka, Bangladesh (South-East Asia region). Expertise in law, policy, and human rights. No conflicts of interest declared. 9. Karima Khalil: Maternal and Child Health Consultant, New Delhi, India (South-East Asia region). Expertise in law, policy, and human rights. No conflicts of interest declared. 10. Primah Kwagala: Director of the Women’s Probono Initiative, Kampala, Uganda (Africa region). Expertise in law, policy, and human rights. No conflicts of interest declared. 11. Monica Arango Olaya: Faculty of Law, University of Oxford, UK (Europe region). Expertise in law, policy, and human rights. No conflicts of interest declared. 12. Xian Warner: Research and Program Coordinator at The Equality Institute, Dili, Timor-Leste (Western Pacific region). Expertise in law, policy, and human rights. No conflicts of interest declared. Additional contributors to the scoping meetings for this domain included Paola Bergallo (University of Torcuato Di Tella, Argentina), Lucia Berro Pizzarossa (University of Groningen, Netherlands), Scott Burris (Temple University, USA), and others.
